source: Original synthetic examples authored for this learning experiment; no real user traces.

knowledge_types.domain: Facts, contracts and constraints about the subject or system, including evidence for them.
knowledge_types.preference: A person or group explicitly states how they want something done.

relations.supports: The incoming statement provides evidence for the candidate.
relations.refines: The incoming statement adds detail or a scoped condition while retaining the candidate.
relations.supersedes: The incoming statement explicitly replaces the candidate in the same scope with authority evidenced in the context.
relations.contradicts: The two statements cannot both hold in the same scope; no replacement is established.
relations.depends_on: The incoming action or procedure requires the candidate as a prerequisite.

cases.title: Evidence supports a contract
cases.incoming: The integration test confirms that create-order returns status 201 when a new order is created.

candidates.text: The create-order API returns 201 for a successful creation.
The dashboard uses a dark theme.

expected.rationale: The test is evidence for the existing API contract. It says nothing about the dashboard theme.

cases.title: A narrower condition
cases.incoming: For duplicate order IDs, create-order returns status 409 rather than creating another order.

candidates.text: The create-order API returns 201 for a successful creation.

expected.rationale: The duplicate case adds a condition; it does not replace the successful-creation contract.

cases.title: A conflict is not a replacement
cases.incoming: The current API specification says a newly created order must return status 200.

candidates.text: The current API specification says a newly created order must return status 201.

expected.rationale: The same scoped contract has incompatible values, with no evidence that either specification supersedes the other.

cases.title: An explicit replacement
cases.incoming: The release owner approved replacing the staging deployment procedure: from now on use the deploy CLI instead of the manual dashboard.

candidates.text: The staging deployment procedure is to use the manual dashboard.

expected.rationale: The event explicitly establishes an authorized replacement for the same environment and procedure.

cases.title: A prerequisite
cases.incoming: Before deploying the staging service, run migration 42 successfully.

candidates.text: Migration 42 creates the table required by the new staging service.

expected.rationale: The incoming deployment procedure requires the existing migration. The directed edge runs from dependent to prerequisite.

cases.title: Similar words, different scope
cases.incoming: The local prototype is deployed by copying its binary into a temporary directory.

candidates.text: Production deployments must use the release pipeline.

expected.rationale: Both mention deployment, but their scopes differ and no semantic relationship is established. Shared vocabulary is not enough.

cases.title: A person changes their preference
cases.incoming: Isaac: I have changed my mind. From now on, use short written updates instead of spoken updates for me.

expected.rationale: The same person explicitly replaces their own communication preference.
The preferences belong to different people; neither contradicts or replaces the other.

cases.title: A scoped exception
cases.incoming: Isaac: For incident handovers, include full details even though my usual updates should stay short.

expected.rationale: The general preference is retained, with an explicit exception for incident handovers.

candidates.text: The disposable prototype uses an in-memory store.

expected.rationale: The instruction is procedural, but "this" does not identify its scope or intended replacement. Do not guess the target.

cases.title: One event supports two facts
cases.incoming: A restart test recovered all acknowledged writes, and recovery completed in 1.2 seconds.

candidates.text: Recovery completes in under two seconds.
The deployment requires an approved release ticket.

expected.rationale: The test provides independent evidence for two claims. It does not establish release approval.

cases.title: A new fact can stand alone
cases.incoming: The export format uses UTF-8 encoding.

expected.rationale: This is a reusable fact with no supplied candidate nodes. An empty candidate set must not force a connection.
